reviews.text: Something is Working. I decided I want to learn all the notes across the guitar fretboard. I am practicing on guitar as mush as possible, but throughout the day I am also getting in mental exercises with this app (I use it without the guitar). It all seems to be working. I am really seeing the fretboard now and the patterns of notes. This app is exactly what I wanted to have. Something simple and fast to practice. And I think it’s really helping me because I definitely can find notes much better than before and am about 80% to knowing the whole fretboard without much hesitation.
Sensitivity. Just so-so, even after adjusting from normal to sensitive, especially on the thinner strings.

worth the upgrade, but some bugs worth acknowledging/ ignoring. sometimes when you let a note ring out, the next interval will pick it up and flag you. mic sometimes flags correct notes. mic sometimes does not pick up notes unless you play loud or face your guitar toward your phone head-on. most of my frustrations with the app revolve around the app either not picking up enough sound, mixed frequencies messing with the detection, or being too sensitive to notes that ring out. don’t quite understand why it won’t recognize the correct note sometimes tho. overall good tool for learning it you stay on top of it and know when to move on (you will prob not master most of the notes because of mic issues).

very helpful. this app is extremely helpful for learning the fretboard! the only issue i’m running into is on the fourth string, the app consistently tells me i am missing B and C, even though i am playing the correct fret and it has no issue recognizing notes below those. there is very little noise and recalibrating did not help

Bad. I’m so disappointed I really wanted to use it but it does not pick up my guitar for some reason and I’m in a quite room only sound is my guitar yet it does not pick it up

Great App may need algorithm work or improved feedback. Overall I love this app because it is exactly how I’ve been trying to practice the fretboard but it takes away two important time lags in that it tells me where new notes are and helps me randomly play one.

I am however currently stuck and I am not sure why… the app says I am playing all the notes correctly and gives no indicators that it is picking up extra noise but at the end of each practice most of my progress bars actually go down? If there is a timing element or if the app thinks I’m playing the wrong note then I feel like that should be given as feedback at the end. It tells you during the lesson if you play the wrong note though so is there a hidden aspect I don’t know about or is the algorithm struggling for some reason?

Edit: I’m reducing my rating. I love this app as a concept but it’s been a couple days and it’s just not useable. I’ve read similar reviews with the EXACT same issues that don’t haven’t seemed to be addressed so until it’s fixed I have to abandoned the app because it no longer serves as a learning tool.

Simply incredible. This app is absolutely great . From the different amount of stringed instruments you can select, to the different tunings you can select as well (and learning notes via different tunings definitely can feel like a mountain to climb) . I’ve had no issues with it thus far, and can easily see myself incorporating this into my practice regiment . If anything, I do catch myself yearning for slightly longer rounds (you can get so into it, it can feel over so quickly), yet there are no complaints for how the app is currently . Definitely an app for our modern times to pick up to feel more comfortable on the fretboard .

Bring back some old features. I started using this app in December and throughly enjoyed it as it was allow me to learn my bass board. Sometime between February-Now is when I’m assuming that the major update and redesign released. I’m writing this review but I see that the dev actually responds to feedback which I am extremely grateful for. 
One feature that I truly miss is the ability to see your progress on notes without pressing “practice”. I used to be able to see my note progression per string, however it doesn’t seem to be the case anymore. Unfortunately you can only see your note progression after each round and even with that, it’s only limited to the notes practiced in a round. I hope in the next update you can bring this feature back as it was extremely useful to me.

Near perfect. This app drills you by telling you what note to play, then listening verify that you play it. It’s exactly how you want to drill yourself to learn the notes of the fretboard. It has all the right options to focus on certain strings and to use sharps and flats. The design is clean, clear and perfectly suited for the task. 

There’s only one problem, and it’s a big one. At first it asks you to find a variety of notes. But after a while, it stops asking about certain notes. Perhaps it is trying to focus on the notes you keep getting wrong, but that doesn’t seem to be the case. So you find yourself being drilled on notes you know, and not learning the other notes you don’t know. 

It would be great if there was a button to clear the training history, so it would ask about all the notes again. Or add an option so it doesn’t try to focus on missed notes

reviews.text: Thanks. …for not asking me to let you track and view my every move on my phone. Other apps request permission to collect all data from your phone all the time which is sleazy. If I open the app once and see that I am being asked to “agree to these terms and conditions”, I will return here, reduce to 1/5 stars. It’s already enough that you DO track certain aspects of my activity. Hence 4/5 stars. Haven’t tried app yet - I’m sure it’s just fine. They’re all the same really. But collection of data is a “Satanic practice”. Ask me once and you get deleted.

Absolute Gamechanger. It’s like flashcards for your fretboard. I’m geeking out over this. It’s perfect. Choose what strings to study, if you want accidentals or not… It says the note out loud so you can just keep your eyes on your fretboard.
I like it. Helpful way to memorize fretboard
More people need to know sbout this app. Helped me memorized my whole fretboard with ease best app ever

Game Changer. Look no further. This is the best. You can even sing the pitch and it will recognize it. The cadence of how long learning notes before adding new ones etc is perfect. I wish I could go back in time and give this to myself first learning guitar. Thanks for making this app!!
fret pro app. I love this app because it tells you which note is which but in the future they could add songs to the app and tell us which notes to play if were trying to learn a certain song

Unhelpful. This is app is really frustrating I paid for the full version because I want to do the whole fretboard but it will still only quiz me on F and G on the low E string. I shouldn’t have to play a G 50 times in a row before it deems that I’ve learned it well enough to start practicing a single other note. It seems functional but I want to be able to use it as practice as an intermediate player not have it assume I’m a beginner who needs to slowly learn every note one at a time.
Also why are there mandatory “rounds”? I get in a rhythm and then my concentration is broken and I find myself looking over at my phone wondering why it stopped going. 
Very overpriced app for how limited it is.

App made by a real human who promptly responded to my email. TAP IN.. I honestly just started to give this app a real try today after having it some few weeks. It has been doing genuine good for me already to help memorization and learning of the fretboard.
The positive stimulus of getting a note correct, in addition to the simplicity and easy navigation of the app set this one apart from all of the other ones I have tried.

Useful, free, and unobtrusive. I really like how this app doesn’t fall into the usual pit-traps of other free apps, there’s no annoying pop-up ads, the UI is visually appealing but simple, and you get a lot of mileage out of what you have free access to. 

You’ll find with how the app works that your practice sessions will become more musical as you begin to memorize the notes better. I think that an app like this could make you feel like you’re just grinding, but fretpro is designed kind of like a musical memory game which makes things more engaging. 

Also, I’ve noticed that the developer(s) are attentive and responsive to feedback which helps me enjoy the app more. I would love if there was a separate mode that would let you memorize the fretboard with just your phone so that you could “practice” while you’re bored on your phone and not near a guitar. This might conflict with the app’s design philosophy, but I’d rather do that over scrolling on socials.
This should be free. Why is this 5$ monthly? At best $1 one time purchase
Almost. If this showed the clef instead of the note name it would be exactly what I need.

Improve the algorithm. With 4 strings selected, it keeps repeating the same notes, which is annoying for even the paid user. It does not suggest notes in a context or randomly. At least 3 times it calls the same notes on the same string.

reviews.text:
Best app for memorizing the fretboard by far!. I’ve been playing guitar for almost 7 years and I have tried many free and paid apps for guitar. this app was a game changer for me and helped me to conquer all of the notes on the fretboard less than a month. It has an efficient UI/UX such that you won’t be disappointed or tired of practicing and It’s environment is very ADHD friendly.
Highly recommended.
As frictionless as scrolling TikTok. Begging you to make a version to learn all the chords too, this app is amazing! Genuinely makes practice 100x easier for me

Great when it works. This app will help with note memorization but I have found that when playing a note the app still thinks it’s wrong. So, I’m here plucking the same string multiple times before it’s accepted. Also, the app will automatically mark the next note wrong because it changes while sound is still ringing out from the previous note. There should be a brief period after each note change where the microphone is not active. This causes me to have to repeat notes I know well more times than necessary.
Fret pro. It was trash don’t recommend
Having fun while getting better. A great app that is getting my fingers and mind in shape.

Still not sold on the subscription model, I understand the creator needs to make living *UPDATED* This app is what I was looking for. If the bugs are fixed, it’d be well worth the money. Running electric guitar into audio interface sometimes it won’t recognize the notes. Sometimes it will ask for a note and then skip right to the next round before I play anything. For a good ten minutes it asked for the same two notes on the same string.

Great Interactive Fretboard Tutor App!. This app challenges you to learn the fretboard by telling you a note on a particular string, and then listening to hear if you got it right. It then tailors the learning based on that. I was previously using a free program that puts the fretboard on the screen and it is so much better to learn by picking the notes on the guitar (duh!)

Refine algorithm & closing brackets?. I’ve noticed that there are some notes that get heavily selected over others in practice, like say on the third (G) string the B note is underdeveloped due to the algorithm choosing that note to be practiced the least. Also should have closed out basically all natural notes from the 6th string but the bar won’t completely fill up, finish, or close out no matter how many times I play a note. Why?

Good Product, Unreasonable Price. The app works as intended, you get a note and have to play it back in order to progress. There are basic features for adjusting difficulty and practice, along with a surprisingly large support for different guitar-esc instruments. Unfortunately, this app is not worth it. The free version is limited heavily to only the first two strings and natural notes. In order to get full access you either need to pay a subscription or a flat 65$ USD (the same price as a console game). You can do the same type of training for free with a note generator site and a tuner. There are similar apps out there that are cheaper and single-purchase.

Great for learning. I have been finding this app very helpful in teaching myself the notes of the fretboard by memory, the app is very easy to use. I only wish my progress was saved across devices so I didn’t have to keep restarting from square one when I use another device.

Wow!!. Exactly what I was looking for… how is this not more popular. Great tool all serious guitar folks should look at. I don’t write a lot of reviews, but enjoyed the simplicity of this app for sure better than my desktop trainer.
amazing. i don’t even pay for music apps but this was well worth it amazing man

Drill, drill, drill. This app is awesome for drilling and learning. As a guitar instructor this app will make its way into my tool bag as a method for helping my students learn the note names and retain what they’ve learned!

Works for me. Despite being in a silent room and tweeting the settings, it sometimes refuses to recognize correct notes. I wish there were some instructions regarding how to make it work better. Despite this complaint, the program does exactly what it promises. It’s an excellent tool to help internalize the fretboard.

The Best Fretboard App. Fred board pro does exactly what I needed to do. I’ve looked in the App Store on and off for years for some thing to help me finally learn the fretboard. This allows me to do as little or as much as I want to do on as many or as few string sets as I want to. I can speak the tones without interference, but still have to follow. It’s random order. Love it. Worth the money.

One Change. The app is great. I’ve been using it constantly. My only change/update is to be able to use the app in landscape mode. Specifically for fret practice mode. Its just tedious scrolling left and right to hit notes when using that feature. Besides that I love this app so much.

Great fretboard learning app!. I’m loving this app simply because it works. I’ve tried to learn the fretboard before, but failed. Brute force memorization just didn’t work for me. Fret Pro simply and patiently drills the note positions into my head a little at a time. I’m very happy with my progress so far. And with that success, continuing is so much easier.

I know other folks have had issues with the app hearing the notes. I read through many of the reviews and tried to learn from them. I’m using an electric guitar with the volume full up and the tone at about half. I’m plugged into an iRig Pro with the gain cranked pretty high. It’s flashing red when I play. The green input bar in the app peaks just about to the top when I play, so the signal is pretty hot. I set the noise suppressor slider high as well. 80% to 90% of full scale. With these settings I’m getting great note detection. Probably 95% or better. 

The note detection isn’t perfect, but I don’t think perfection is a fair expectation. I expect the app to help me learn notes. And it does. 

I’m looking forward to new features like mentioned by other users. For me, I’d like to see an option to practice each string either from open to fret 11, as it is now, or from fret 1 to fret 12. I would also love to be able to select individual notes to practice across all 6 strings.

Thanks again for a great learning tool!

Finally, I’m learning the fretboard!. Been looking for an app just like this! It is almost perfect! Tried others, but never stuck with them. Didn’t need the lifetime license (once you learn it, you’ve learned it, right?) but did it to give a thanks for creating such an awesome app.

This works great, don’t waste money on others or books. Asked for a change from the app maker and he was right on it with an update. 
Really the best working tool to actually memorize the fretboard quickly. 

Been playing since age 7 and never did it. 
Now inside of a week,
I am well on my way to crushing every single note on the entire board …on my 8 strings. 

Thank you, Ryan!!
Just doesn’t work. I’m playing the correct note. My guitar is tuned correctly. The app doesn’t care. Wasted my time.
Top notch.. If you get premium (which is very, very affordable!), you get a very useful app that tracks your progress, tests you, and challenges you. Fantastic app, simple but great.

Solid training, needs better not recognition. Like other reviewers have written, this is a great app for training fret board notes. However, it struggles with note recognition. I’ve tried all the mic settings and a couple different acoustic guitars, but too often it won’t pick up the right note. I’ve even tried connecting directly through a headphone amp (Fender micro) on my electric and it still struggles. It’s pretty frustrating and ruins the pacing of practice.

The best fretboard learner on the market but could be improved. This app is the best app for learning the fretboard as of now but a future competitor can implement certain things that will have it beat. I hope the developer will add these things so it can remain on top.

1. The app requests me to play the note E. There is a million different ways to play an E on the guitar. As of right now, the app doesn’t differentiate between the E’s it wants me to play aside from telling me I played the wrong E even if I still played an E. There should be a symbol next to the E to signify which E I should be playing. This part of the app is very frustrating and makes the learning experience much more tedious than it has to be. 

2. There should be a feature to memorize the different chords on the guitar, similar to the system used for learning the fretboard.
great. simple and effective

Awesome app. Very useful for learning the fretboard. Would definitely recommend, especially if you’ve already learned scale shapes. Memorizing note names is kind of like eating your vegetables, but this app has done a great job at breaking it up into easily manageable bite size pieces. Effective and kind of addicting 😆

Great concept, but…. The app makes too many mistakes. I have tried multiple guitars, two ipads and adjusted the background filter settings and different input location settings for the microphone, but nonetheless about every 5th to 10th input it will either: a. flash red like I misplayed the note immediately before I even get a chance to play the note, b. not recognize that I am playing the correct note, even though my guitar is in tune and the app itself shows I am playing the correct note when I go into the settings, c. get stuck where it won’t move off a note and won’t turn green or red, but just flash gray like I am not playing at a high enough volume. I can clear this by telling it to show the fretboard and playing the note there and then going through the steps to hide the fretboard but that is very tedious. Also, on one of my ipads, if I exit back to the main screen and then come back later to play, it can’t pick up any guitar sounds unless I swipe the app closed and reopen it. I would switch to five stars if these problems could be fixed.

UPDATING: At the developer’s suggestion I upped the bass knob on my amp and turned down the treble and mid range and that mostly fixed things. I think the app will now help me upgrade my reasonable fret board knowledge to my goal of locating the notes without any conscious thought or effort.

40 dollars for unlocking the app.... 40 dollars is too high of an ask for this basic of an app. Or you can do a monthly payment, like every other app asks for nowadays. Monthly payment doesn't even makes sense for this type of app, it's greedy.

Update: Still Perfect Fretboard Drills App!. The latest update is a nice improvement. As I’ve improved my note-finding, speed has become more important. This new version is faster, and since it respects the Accessibility voice settings, I get an even faster drills session. 

Original review:
It does its one-thing really well: help you gradually develop muscle-memory across the fretboard. It’s easy to imagine a tennis coach spending 20 minutes with a player on drills shot after shot. But I can’t imagine a guitar coach spending even 10 minutes on play-this-note, play-that-note drills. This app is that coach, running drills and giving feedback. I’ve had lessons on-and-off for 10 years, but never did the work of really knowing the notes on the fretboard. I didn’t think it really mattered. But now, concepts I slightly understood before are falling into place, and I’m able to communicate with my teacher in the same language. Recommended.
Concept is just what I wanted. But IPhone mic doesn’t seem to pick up correct notes played even though GuitarTuna tuner has no trouble identifying notes through same mic.

Effective training method. I’ve been playing guitar about 18 months but struggled with learning notes’ names. For about a week, I spent an hour a day with this app. It gets tedious. But it’s effective. Now that I know the notes, it’s like a superpower!

Excellent!. As a beginner to intermediate guitar player, this is a great tool… as someone who writes software for a living, this is a really thoughtful and well crafted app with beautiful font choices, great use of animation and real feature richness. I’m really pleased!
Wonderfully done. So much appreciated. The practical way this is designed and makes you work on mistakes
Works great. Worth the money to upgrade, like flash cards for your fretboard.

Best Fretboard Memorization App. I pulled down all of the apps in this category and tried them all out and this was the best of them. I like how it’s a one time purchase for full features, at a reasonable price. I love how it works with audio interfaces as well as the mic to recognize your notes and the recognition is spot on and fast (at least through audio interface which is what I use). The developer is responsive to suggestions and is still actively enhancing this app. 

What I’d like to see in future releases is support for custom tunings, support for all frets and/or a custom selection of frets and/or notes, as well as the ability to configure note recognition to accept any octave of the given note so that you could for instance be prompted to play E and it would accept any octave of E allowing you to jump around or play the same not in a higher octave on the same string. Also a more specific configuration would be cool where it could also prompt for a very specific note such as E3 (E in the third octave) where your be memorizing not only the notes but also their octave.

Used to be a stellar way to learn the fretboard. This app used to be worked into my daily practice routine. It did everything you needed it to. Every other fretboard learning tool has you identity notes on your phone. This app lets you play it on your guitar, which helps with memorization. However, in recent months something has happened with the app so that it doesn’t work properly. If I don’t play a note within 2 seconds it will register as a wrong note, and it will keep doing this repeatedly, even if you do hit the right note it is in a continuous loop of marking a wrong note. I’ve tried messing with a lot of the settings, adjusting the microphone sensitivity, and using different devices, but nothing works. It makes it very hard and frustrating to use. Before this bug, I would have given it 5 stars. However, it’s almost unusable now. I wouldn’t purchase the full version until it is fixed. I really hope the developer is able to fix it soon, because it used to be my favorite fretboard training app.

For $5 needs much improvement. I was excited at the potential of your app, yet for $5 it can use some much needed features. Here are some suggestions for improvement.

Mic sensitivity
I moved the sensitivity all the way up and I have to pluck a note 3 or 4 times sometimes for it to read the sound.

Adjustable timer
A timer that users can set so we can track our progress. For example, having an adjustable timer from 1 - 30 seconds per note. So if I wanted to have 11 seconds to figure out each note or notes in different parts of the fretboard, after 11 seconds it would move on automatically to the next note and give me 11 seconds and so on. This way after a week or so I could change the timer to 8 seconds per note and a few weeks after that 5 seconds per note to see how my speed in finding notes is improving.

Reveal location
A switch that allows us to turn off the feature that tells us where the note is. Currently it tells you where it is after just one mistake. I want to have the choice to either see it or not see it at all.

Read notes everywhere
When told to find an E note, say on the 6th string, it will only accept the open E string as an answer, the E on the 12th fret is valid but your app doesn’t recognize it. This should be programmed to find an E note anywhere on the string and if you want to pick both it should accept both.

String Selection

I selected all strings and then when that ended I selected strings 1 - 3. Both times, when I started to practice it became evident that the app was only cycling through a couple of strings and only some of the natural notes, even though I turned off Natural Notes Only. It would be better if it cycled through all the notes or gave you the option to focus on a handful of notes.

Please consider implementing these suggestions.

Great design & better learning. FretPro is a great app! The simple design and minimal setup got me up and running fast, frustration-free. I’m new to guitar but FretPro has considerably flattened the learning curve over time.

Learn notes fast!. I would consider myself a beginner guitar player (I’ve been learning for about a year and a half) and I was able to memorize the notes on the 4th, 5th and 6th string within just a couple weeks using this app for a few minutes everyday during my guitar practice. I like that you can just sit down with your guitar, open up the app and immediately get to work. It makes learning the notes along the fretboard much more manageable by breaking it down into chunks and quizzing you over and over again until it knows you’ve got it down. The app is really easy to use and intuitive.
Amazing Production & Learning Tool (Highly Recommend). This app is an instant favorite. Helping me learn and add to my production game. A great Production & Learning Tool (Highly Recommend)!

great app, missing one thing. great app, does what it should do but notifications are a must. i want to practice my notes daily but often forget, being able to have the option to have prompting notifications on the days of the week you select would be a great update !

New version has removed critical features. I’ve been using this app every day to try to learn the notes of the guitar. Today I opened it up and it had a new version. It seems cool but it’s missing two critical features

- it no longer shows the answer if you get it wrong a few times. Without this feature the app is really hard to use for me

Love this app. I downloaded it, immediately upgraded to pro and I was off! I train with it for 10 minutes a day and it’s already helping my fluency on the fretboard. It’s also really helpful to see where you’re at with each note on the dashboard. For further gamification I’d love to see what the levels (“learning” vs “practicing” vs “mastered”) mean inside the app and maybe even have additional levels added.

Helpful when it works. I often use this app and even paid for the subscription to use all strings even though i find it slightly expensive. my personal favourite feature was the option to have the notes spoken to you as it’s clear what string you are playing on. however, whenever i click on this feature, the chances of it actually working are slim. Liked it at first. I liked the idea of the app at first but once I did the free trial, it seemed I only had one exercise I could do which was learn all the notes on the fret board. I was hoping to be able to jump around between that and scale exercises, but it seems you can only gain access to those features later? I dunno it seemed pretty limited for 6$ CAD /month service. Not worth it IMO.

Great idea, decent execution. Overall a fun app, have only tried the free stuff so far but a couple of annoying things i kept running into that tweaking slightly would make the app even better!

Note tracking was good but when you play a note it immediately switches to requesting the next note and tells you it’s incorrect because you’re playing the last note requested. Might be cool if it buffered the next note slightly but i guess that could annoy people who care about being timed more than actually learning

Also if you’re supposed to be playing an octave of an open note it doesn’t distinguish if it should be the 12th or 24th fret, it only gives you the generic 12+ symbol. So again I’m being told I’m making mistakes when it’s really just information not being communicated clearly. Don’t know an elegant solution to this, having a 24+ symbol would king of just be telling you exactly what fret to play and kind of defeats the purpose. Maybe labeling fret 0-11 as octave 1 12-23 as octave 2 and 24+ as octave 3 could mitigate this issue?

Superb app. This app opened my eyes to the fretboard like some type of revelation!! Super super helpful. I definitely recommend 100/10! I spoke to the developer Ryan, he was so gracious to respond to all my questions and suggestions. Very great job Ryan!

Most useful guitar app I own. I have wanted to learn the notes on my front board for over 20 years. I have triedOther methods with varying success. In the end this has been the most effective system I’ve used. It takes care of all the work of keeping track of which notes I know well and which ones are new for me. It calls out the notes and I just got to play as it listens to see if I get it correct. This is a really fun way to learn the notes on the fretboard.
